entities.summary: Ya\u02c9qūb ibn یāriq was a Persian astronomer and mathematician who lived in Baghdad, a city that served as the capital of the Abbasid Caliphate, a center of Islamic learning and culture that attracted scholars from all over the world. During his lifetime, ibn ˉriq made significant contributions to the field of astronomy, including the development of a new system of astronomical tables that was used for centuries. His work was widely influential and helped to shape the course of Islamic scholarship and the development of astronomy in the Middle East. The legacy of ibn ˉriq can be seen in the many astronomers and mathematicians who followed in his footsteps, including Ibn Yunus and Al-Biruni. In 796 CE, ibn ˉriq passed away, leaving behind a body of work that continues to be studied and admired by scholars today.

entities.summary: Yaʿqūb ibn Ṭāriq was a Persian astronomer and mathematician who lived in Baghdad, where he made significant contributions to the field of astronomy during the Abbasid Caliphate. Born in 800 CE, Yaʿqūb ibn Ṭāriq was part of a circle of scholars who sought to revive ancient Greek knowledge and make it compatible with Islamic theology. His most notable work is the book "Kitab al-madkhal li tabqī‘ al-ḥay‘a wa al-ḥay‘a al-rasīmiyya", which provides a detailed explanation of the principles of astronomy and mathematics. Yaʿqūb ibn Ṭāriq's work had a lasting impact on the development of astronomy in the Islamic world, influencing later scholars such as Ibn Yunus and Al-Zarqali. Despite his significant contributions, Yaʿqūb ibn Ṭāriq's life was cut short, and he died in 796 CE at the age of 26. His legacy, however, continues to be celebrated by scholars and historians today.
